title: Acyclic resolutions compute derived section maps on ringed sites
statement:
Let $\mathcal C,\mathcal D$ be small sites with terminal objects in a common coefficient universe [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology, def-weil-size-convention], equipped with sheaves of commutative rings $A,B$. Let $f:(\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C),A)\to(\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal D),B)$ be a morphism of ringed topoi [def-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-morphism]. Assume the two module categories [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] have enough injectives [def-sp-enough-injectives]. Let $M$ be a $B$-module, $N$ an $A$-module and $\phi:M\to f_*N$ a module map. Suppose $r:M[0]\to K$ and $s:N[0]\to L$ are augmented resolutions, zero in negative degrees, with every term acyclic for the respective global-section functor, meaning $R^p\Gamma(\mathcal D,K^q)=R^p\Gamma(\mathcal C,L^q)=0$ for $p>0$ [def-sp-injective-resolutions, def-sp-acyclic]. Let $u:K\to f_*L$ be a chain map with $u r=(f_*s)\phi[0]$. Write $Q$ for localization at quasi-isomorphisms [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Use the bounded-below derived category $D^+(\operatorname{Ab})$ [def-weil-pbc-bounded-derived-subcategories]. There are canonical isomorphisms in this category,
$$c_r:Q\Gamma(\mathcal D,K)\xrightarrow{\sim}R\Gamma(\mathcal D,M),\qquad c_s:Q\Gamma(\mathcal C,L)\xrightarrow{\sim}R\Gamma(\mathcal C,N).$$
They are the acyclic-resolution comparisons: if $K\to I$ extends $r$ into an injective resolution of $M$, $c_r$ is its image on derived sections followed by the injective-resolution computation; likewise for $c_s$. These comparisons are independent of the extensions. Under $\Gamma(\mathcal D,f_*L)=\Gamma(\mathcal C,L)$ one has an equality of derived morphisms
$$c_s\,Q\Gamma(u)=\operatorname{res}_f(\phi)\,c_r,$$
where $\operatorname{res}_f(\phi)$ is $R\Gamma$ of the map $M[0]\to Rf_*(N[0])$ induced by $\phi$, followed by the canonical composition comparison $R\Gamma(\mathcal D,Rf_*N)\cong R\Gamma(\mathcal C,N)$. In particular the canonical coefficient-compatible pullback maps are computed by augmentation-preserving maps between these acyclic resolutions, as morphisms in the derived category before taking any cohomology. For $f=\mathrm{id}$ the same formula gives naturality for all augmentation-preserving maps of resolutions. No exactness of $f^*$ or injectivity of the terms of $K,L$ is assumed.

proof.text: Write $G=\Gamma(\mathcal D,-)$ and $H=\Gamma(\mathcal C,-)$, valued in abelian groups. They are additive and left exact: kernels of module sheaves are sectionwise, and sections over the terminal object preserve these kernels. Choose nonnegative injective resolutions $i:M[0]\to J$ and $j:N[0]\to I$. The bounded-below injective complexes $I,J$ are K-injective. The small ringed-site module categories admit K-injective resolutions, so use their total derived functors and canonical units. Write $\rho_J:RG(M[0])\xrightarrow{\sim}QGJ$ and $\rho_I:RH(N[0])\xrightarrow{\sim}QHI$ for the unit-normalized resolution computations.

The augmentation $r$ is a degreewise monomorphic quasi-isomorphism: its degree-zero component identifies $M$ with the kernel of $K^0\to K^1$, and its other components have zero source. Extend $i$ across $r$ into $J$ to obtain $a:K\to J$ with $ar=i$; likewise obtain $b:L\to I$ with $bs=j$. Any two extensions into the fixed target are homotopic, by uniqueness along a quasi-isomorphism. Both $a,b$ are quasi-isomorphisms, since on cohomology their composites with the quasi-isomorphisms $r,s$ are $i,j$.

source.place: Tag 013P (lemma-morphisms-lift), part (2), and uniqueness preceding that lemma

proof.text:
Injective module sheaves are section-acyclic, by the injective-pushforward global-acyclicity lemma with the identity ringed-topos morphism. Thus the source and target terms of $a$ are $G$-acyclic, and those of $b$ are $H$-acyclic. The acyclic quasi-isomorphism lemma gives quasi-isomorphisms $G(a)$ and $H(b)$. Consequently
$$c_r=\rho_J^{-1}\,QG(a),\qquad c_s=\rho_I^{-1}\,QH(b)$$
are isomorphisms in $D^+(\operatorname{Ab})$. These are precisely the comparisons specified in the statement, since $a,b$ extend the augmentations into injective resolutions.

Applying an additive functor to a chain homotopy again gives a chain homotopy. Since localization factors through the homotopy category, $QG(a)$ and $QH(b)$ are independent of the extensions. To compare $i:M[0]\to J$ with another nonnegative injective resolution $i':M[0]\to J'$, represent $Qi'(Qi)^{-1}$ by a chain map $t:J\to J'$ using the K-injective Hom bijection. Then $ti\simeq i'$ and hence $ta\simeq a'$ by uniqueness after precomposition with $r$. The normalized derived-map computation gives $\rho_{J'}=QG(t)\rho_J$. Thus
$$\rho_{J'}^{-1}QG(a')=\rho_{J'}^{-1}QG(t)QG(a)=\rho_J^{-1}QG(a).$$
The identical argument with $H,s,I$ gives independence for $c_s$.

Choose a quasi-isomorphism $\lambda:f_*I\to T$ with $T$ bounded below and termwise injective. Each $f_*I^q$ is $G$-acyclic by the ringed-topos injective-pushforward lemma, without flatness. The terms of $T$ are also $G$-acyclic by that lemma for the identity morphism. Apply the acyclic quasi-isomorphism lemma, taking a common lower bound for $f_*I,T$, to see that $E=QG(\lambda)$ is invertible. Put $\rho_T:RG(Qf_*I)\xrightarrow{\sim}QGT$. The normalized derived-composition comparison identifies
$$RG(Qf_*I)\longrightarrow QHI=QG(f_*I)$$
with $E^{-1}\rho_T$. Indeed, apply its K-injective representative formula to $I$ and $\lambda$, taking the second ringed-topos morphism to be global sections to $(\operatorname{Set},\mathbf Z)$. Its module direct image is exactly $G$; the formula for the comparison in the other direction is $QG(\lambda)=E$.

Let $w=(f_*j)\phi[0]:M[0]\to f_*I$. Under the resolution computation $Rf_*N\cong Qf_*I$, the morphism induced by $\phi$ is $Qw$: this is naturality of the derived unit $Qf_*\Rightarrow Rf_*Q$ at $j$. By the K-injective Hom bijection, choose $\beta:J\to T$ representing
$$Q\beta=Q\lambda\,Qw\,(Qi)^{-1}.$$
The same bijection implies $\beta i\simeq\lambda w$. With $V=QG(\beta)$, computation of derived morphisms on the resolutions $i,\lambda$, followed by Step 5's normalized composition comparison, gives the precise coordinate formula
$$\rho_I\,\operatorname{res}_f(\phi)\,\rho_J^{-1}=E^{-1}V.$$
Here the functor computing $Rf_*$ is module direct image; no injectivity claim about $f_*I$ is used.

source.place: Tag 070Y (lemma-K-injective-defined) and sites-cohomology.tex section-derived-functors; Tag 0D6E normalization from Step 5

proof.text:
The two maps $\lambda(f_*b)u,\beta a:K\to T$ agree up to homotopy after precomposition with $r$: using $ur=(f_*s)\phi[0]$, $bs=j$, and $ar=i$, their composites are $\lambda(f_*j)\phi[0]=\lambda w$ and $\beta i\simeq\lambda w$. The target $T$ is bounded below and termwise injective. Uniqueness along the quasi-isomorphism $r$ therefore makes these maps homotopic. Apply $G$ to that homotopy and localize. Naturality of the section identity $Gf_*=H$ then gives the equality of derived morphisms
$$E\,QH(b)\,Q\Gamma(u)=V\,QG(a).$$

Multiply the last equality by $\rho_I^{-1}E^{-1}$ on the left. Substitution of Steps 3 and 6 yields
$$c_s\,Q\Gamma(u)=\rho_I^{-1}E^{-1}VQG(a)=\operatorname{res}_f(\phi)\,c_r.$$
All terms lie in $D^+(\operatorname{Ab})$: the section complexes and injective replacements used are bounded below. Step 4 supplies all comparison independence. Substitution $f=\mathrm{id}$ gives naturality for every augmentation-preserving map; substitution of a specified coefficient-compatible pullback and its coefficient map gives the asserted computation. These are substitutions in the derived equality, before applying any cohomology functor.
